citation: Sutton, R. S. (1990). Integrated Architectures for Learning, Planning, and Reacting Based on Approximating Dynamic Programming. Proceedings of the Seventh International Conference on Machine Learning, 216-224.
use: Foundational integration of learned models, planning, and reinforcement learning. The present planner is related to Dyna but is not a reproduction of Dyna-Q.

citation: Vitter, J. S. (1985). Random Sampling with a Reservoir. ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software, 11(1), 37-57.
use: Reservoir sampling baseline uses Algorithm R, not the paper's faster Algorithm Z.

citation: Isele, D., and Cosgun, A. (2018). Selective Experience Replay for Lifelong Learning. Proceedings of AAAI, 32(1), 3302-3309.
use: Prior work compares experience selection by distribution and coverage. Coverage-based selection is not claimed as a new idea.

citation: Agarwal, R., Schwarzer, M., Castro, P. S., Courville, A., and Bellemare, M. G. (2021). Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 34.
use: Motivates reporting uncertainty across training runs. This study uses its own paired bootstrap implementation, not the rliable package.

citation: Yao, S., Zhao, J., Yu, D., Du, N., Shafran, I., Narasimhan, K., and Cao, Y. (2023). ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models. International Conference on Learning Representations.
use: Established language-agent reasoning and action loop; conceptual application context only.

citation: Shinn, N., Cassano, F., Berman, E., Gopinath, A., Narasimhan, K., and Yao, S. (2023). Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning. arXiv:2303.11366, version 4.
use: Experience and reflective memory can support adaptation without weight updates; does not validate this study's LLM proposal.

citation: Zhou, A., Yan, K., Shlapentokh-Rothman, M., Wang, H., and Wang, Y.-X. (2024). Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning in Language Models. Proceedings of ICML, PMLR 235, 62138-62160.
use: Planning in language agents is established; search cost must be measured.

citation: Kapoor, S., Stroebl, B., Siegel, Z. S., Nadgir, N., and Narayanan, A. (2024). AI Agents That Matter. arXiv:2407.01502.
use: Motivates joint reporting of accuracy and cost and attention to held-out evaluation.

citation: Liu, N. F., Lin, K., Hewitt, J., Paranjape, A., Bevilacqua, M., Petroni, F., and Liang, P. (2023). Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts. arXiv:2307.03172, version 3.
use: Specific long-context retrieval failures motivate testing memory presentation. The findings are not a claim that larger training datasets inherently harm models.
